From 323156c3541e23da7e582008a7ac30cd51b60acd Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Emmanuel Grumbach <emmanuel.grumbach@intel.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 11:33:25 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] wifi: iwlwifi: mvm: don't send a 6E related command when not
 supported

MCC_ALLOWED_AP_TYPE_CMD is related to 6E support. Do not send it if the
device doesn't support 6E.
Apparently, the firmware is mistakenly advertising support for this
command even on AX201 which does not support 6E and then the firmware
crashes.

Fixes: 0d2fc8821a7d ("wifi: iwlwifi: nvm: parse the VLP/AFC bit from regulatory")
Closes: https://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=220804
Signed-off-by: Emmanuel Grumbach <emmanuel.grumbach@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Johannes Berg <johannes.berg@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Miri Korenblit <miriam.rachel.korenblit@intel.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260324113316.e171f0163f2a.I0c444d1f82d1773054e7ffc391ad49697d58f44e@changeid

diff --git a/drivers/net/wireless/intel/iwlwifi/mvm/fw.c b/drivers/net/wireless/intel/iwlwifi/mvm/fw.c
index 43cf94c9a36b..6cc78661116e 100644
--- a/drivers/net/wireless/intel/iwlwifi/mvm/fw.c
+++ b/drivers/net/wireless/intel/iwlwifi/mvm/fw.c
@@ -470,7 +470,8 @@ static void iwl_mvm_uats_init(struct iwl_mvm *mvm)
 		.dataflags[0] = IWL_HCMD_DFL_NOCOPY,
 	};
 
-	if (mvm->trans->mac_cfg->device_family < IWL_DEVICE_FAMILY_AX210) {
+	if (mvm->trans->mac_cfg->device_family < IWL_DEVICE_FAMILY_AX210 ||
+	    !mvm->trans->cfg->uhb_supported) {
 		IWL_DEBUG_RADIO(mvm, "UATS feature is not supported\n");
 		return;
 	}
-- 
2.34.1

### Summary of Modifications

#### Modifications in Each File

- **`drivers/net/wireless/intel/iwlwifi/mvm/fw.c`**:
  - In the function `iwl_mvm_uats_init`, the existing conditional check for device family (`device_family < IWL_DEVICE_FAMILY_AX210`) was extended.  
  - Added a logical OR condition: `!mvm->trans->cfg->uhb_supported`.  
  - This means the function now returns early (skipping the `MCC_ALLOWED_AP_TYPE_CMD` command) if either:  
    - The device is older than AX210, **or**  
    - The device does not support UHB (6 GHz / 6E) even if it is AX210 or newer.

#### Relationships Between Changes

- The bug occurred because the firmware on certain devices (e.g., AX201) incorrectly advertises support for the `MCC_ALLOWED_AP_TYPE_CMD` command, even though the hardware does not support 6E.  
- The original check only filtered by device family (AX210+), which was insufficient because some devices in that family (like AX201) lack 6E capability.  
- Adding the `uhb_supported` flag check ensures the command is only sent when the device truly supports 6E, preventing the firmware crash reported in the bug.  
- This is a minimal, targeted fix that avoids altering the command handling logic for other valid cases.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
if (mvm->trans->mac_cfg->device_family < IWL_DEVICE_FAMILY_AX210) {
Reason:
The condition only checked if the device family is at least AX210, but did not verify whether the device actually supports 6E (UHB). Some devices in or above that family (e.g., AX201) do not support 6E, yet their firmware may incorrectly advertise support for the MCC_ALLOWED_AP_TYPE_CMD. Sending the command to such devices causes a firmware crash.  

The code statements that fix the bug are:
if (mvm->trans->mac_cfg->device_family < IWL_DEVICE_FAMILY_AX210 ||
    !mvm->trans->cfg->uhb_supported) {
Reason:
The fix adds a check for `!mvm->trans->cfg->uhb_supported`. This ensures that even if the device family is high enough, the command is not sent when the device lacks 6E support. The early return prevents the firmware crash by avoiding the command entirely on devices that should not receive it.
